function.name: reqmap_init
function.description: First-use bootstrap: scaffold requirements/ and .reqmapignore if missing, draft requirements from existing code and prose, build the lock and map, and print guided next steps. Idempotent — safe to re-run; never clobbers an existing .reqmapignore. --plan emits the extraction plan as JSON and writes no requirement files, for looking before authoring.

root.description: Repo root where requirements/ lives; defaults to the current directory.

plan.description: Emit the extraction plan as JSON instead of writing requirement files.

out.description: With --plan: write the plan JSON here ('-' or omitted = stdout).

md_glob.description: With --plan: also scan these non-code globs for capabilities (repeatable).

wipe.description: Hard-reset: delete all non-generated requirements and strip membership tags from source files before re-extracting.

no_site.description: Skip the final site step (scaffolding docs/architecture.html).

function.name: reqmap_new
function.description: Scaffold a new blank requirement from the built-in template. Use --from-todo and --id together to pre-fill from a TODO.md item instead.

root.description: Repo root where requirements/ lives; defaults to the current directory.

id.description: Requirement ID in AREA-NAME-NNN format (e.g. AUTH-LOGIN-001). Required when using --from-todo.

from_todo.description: Scaffold the requirement from a TODO.md item matched by this name (use with --id; add --mark-done to flip the item to [x]).

mark_done.description: Also flip the matched TODO.md item to [x] (off by default). Only used with --from-todo.

function.name: reqmap_gate
function.description: The commit/CI verdict, and every read-only question you can ask the corpus. Bare, it verifies that every code tag resolves to a real requirement, that every confirmed requirement has at least one implements: member, and that drift has not been introduced since the last sync, then checks requirement readability and map freshness. Exits non-zero on link-sync errors only. Never writes anything. The mode flags answer one question each instead of running the verdict: --audit for the whole problem report, --risk for what to do next, --show for one requirement's dossier, --search to rank by relevance, --dupes for overlapping contracts, --design for the code review, --review and --implement for the two machine-readable plans.

root.description: Repo root where requirements/ lives; defaults to the current directory.

mode_audit.description: Print every pass that discovers a problem as one report: the gate, corpus risk, duplicate contracts, design signals and tag coverage. The exit code still comes from the gate alone.

mode_risk.description: Print the corpus risk snapshot and the actionable signals, most urgent first.

mode_show.description: Print one requirement's dossier: intent, contract, dependencies both ways, code members with file:line, open questions and risk signals.

mode_search.description: Rank requirements by lexical relevance to a free-text query.

mode_dupes.description: Rank requirement pairs whose contracts overlap, most similar first.

mode_design.description: Print the advisory design review of the code. Never part of the verdict.

mode_review.description: Emit the deterministic review plan for one requirement, as JSON.

mode_implement.description: Emit the implementation brief for one requirement: obligations, required tags, similar existing code.

show_all.description: With --risk: expand every bucket instead of the top few.

untagged.description: With --risk: report membership-tag coverage per directory.

as_badge.description: With --risk: print the coherence score as a badge string.

top.description: With --search or --dupes: how many results to print.

strict.description: Promote drift and test-link integrity warnings to errors. Useful in CI when all requirements are confirmed.

json.description: Emit structured JSON output instead of human-readable text.

since.description: Scope the gate to requirements whose member files changed since this git ref (e.g. 'main', 'HEAD~1').

function.name: reqmap_sync
function.description: The write path. Rescan code members, advance the drift baseline, and regenerate the map, the findings file and the generated integration artifacts in one step. Run after editing requirement files or tagging new code members. --accept-drift is required when a confirmed or implemented contract changed. --suggest-verifies proposes per-criterion verifies: tags, and writes them with --apply.

root.description: Repo root where requirements/ lives; defaults to the current directory.

mode_retire.description: Take these requirements out of service instead of confirming them. Accepts one id or many; a batch retires in an order computed from the graph, under one working-tree check. Prints the blast radius; writes nothing without --apply.

delete.description: With --retire: also remove the block, its lock entries and its membership tags. Never a function body.

do_apply.description: With --retire or --suggest-verifies: actually write the change. Without it, the run is a dry report.

force.description: With --retire: proceed even though dependents still point at this requirement, or the working tree is dirty. Dependents that are already deprecated, and those retired in the same call, never block.

mode_suggest.description: Propose per-criterion `verifies:` tags for tests already named after the criterion they check.

findings.description: Also regenerate the aggregated open-questions file.

accept_drift.description: Explicitly advance the baseline when a confirmed or implemented contract changed. Required when those contracts differ from the lock; sync exits non-zero without it. Takes an optional reason, recorded in requirements/_driftlog.json so the waiver and its justification land in the diff.

strict.description: Promote drift and test-link integrity from warn to error.

function.name: reqmap_clarify
function.description: Ask what a requirement has not answered yet: vague terms with no threshold, numbers with no unit, unbounded quantities, clauses with no case, a missing failure path. Read-only, always exit 0, never a gate rule. --decompose is the write half of the same question: it splits a requirement into code-rung children along the bold group labels in its Description (--apply writes), or scaffolds one draft per over-long clause when it has none. Run it before implementing, so the ambiguity is resolved in the requirement instead of guessed in code.

root.description: Repo root where requirements/ lives; defaults to the current directory.

decompose.description: Split a requirement into code-rung children along the bold group labels its author wrote in the Description; --apply writes them and rewrites the parent. With no id, every requirement carrying groups. A requirement with no groups falls back to one draft per over-long clause.

levels.description: Propose a V-model rung for every requirement that declares no `level:`; --apply writes them, each marked `level_source: auto`.

as_json.description: Emit the questions as JSON for an agent to answer.
